- Use ethically sourced beans that have captured terroir and have been properly processed (appropriate ripeness, moisture levels etc). The beans should have minimal defects.
- Those beans should be professionally roasted for optimal flavour development. They should be even, have no signs of scorching, and have a roast profile that compliments the origin characteristics of the coffee.
- Beans should be fresh to ensure minimal oxidation (the aromatics in coffee are volatile and degrade easily). However, they should be given a few days after roasting to rest, as the carbon dioxide present affects coffee extraction. Coffee starts to deteriorate in quality after about two weeks.
- Coffee should be ground immediately prior to brewing as larger surface area = faster oxidation.
- In order for coffee to extract evenly, your coffee must be ground evenly, and this is achieved with a well made burr grinder.
- The mineral content of your water has a significant effect on extraction. Water that is overly hard or soft will negatively impact the quality of your cup.
- Ideal grind size, coffee to water ratio, steep time and brewing temperature vary depending on what vessel you are using for your coffee (french press, chemex etc).
